text:
You can clearly see it's more than 2 slots thick. You couldn't put a PCI-E card next to it, not even a super low profile Wifi adapter or anything. It's amazing that a "reviewer" could hold the card physically in his hands and not be able to see how thick it is...

On the other hand, the ASROCK RX6700XT is actually 2 slots thick and destroys this POS at the same price right now.
author: @iancurrie8844

text: I see your point, we were looking at it from the viewpoint of how many PCIe covers you would have to remove to fit the card. We will definitely keep that in mind with our next review. Thanks for the feedback
author: @WeDoTech

text:
@WeDoTech  Ah. Well, "slots" refers to pci express (or PCI or ISA) slots it covers and cannot be used. It's a 3 slot cooler ;)

They design it this way specifically so that the third slot cannot be used so that the fans have enough room to draw air. Regarless of the back plates, it consumes 3 slots by design.
author: @iancurrie8844

text: @iancurrie8844  makes sense, will check into it thanks!
author: @WeDoTech

text: FYI, it is NOT a 3 slot cooler and you CAN put a PCI-E card in next to it. It's 2.5 slots wide max, and I've got an old Sound card sat next to this very 4060 in my PC andnd there's perfectly enough space for everything to fit without blocking any fans.
author: @Groovy-Train

text: @Groovy-Train   If it's 2.5 slots wide, then it's 3 slots. This is obvious to anyone with any critical thinking skills. It occupies 3 slots that cannot be used for anything else.
author: @iancurrie8844

text: @iancurrie8844  If you have a two slot video card, anyone with critical thinking skills knows you would not put a pci-e card in a slot right next to it, therefore blocking it's fans and cooling capability. That would just be stupid!
author: @Groovy-Train

text: ​ @Groovy-Train   Actually there are very low profile M.2 adapters which would be fine. it's 2.5 which means it's a 3 slot card. You cannot use half a slot.
